newsitem.title: UK: Med gasoline, naphtha rise in line with crude oil.
newsitem.headline: Med gasoline, naphtha rise in line with crude oil.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Monday, traders said.

Gasoline prices edged higher on the back of firmer crude and with NYMEX unleaded futures holding small gains, but traders said lengthy supplies particularly of low octane material were capping the market.
Delivered Eurograde cargoes were talked around 50 cents to $1 per tonne firmer at $193/$196.
Naphtha prices were slightly firmer with crude but traders said end-user demand was still very thin.
Moroccan barrels were still seen available at what some traders said was a high, pricing related, offer of $177 a tonne and expected to see little buying interest for the material.
They said Algerian fourth quarter term contract pricing was keeping sellers levels artificially high.
"The Moroccan barrels have been there since early last week but the price is more related to the Q4 pricing rather and is not an indication of any real strength," a trader said.
Best bids were notionally assessed $4-5 below this level.
The last cargoes of June delivery EN590 material went at the end of last week with the sellers saying they achieved in excess of quotes fob hi +$3.0.

Traders said they thought low sulphur would remain firm over the coming week. "We're still waiting for our July programme but we've had plenty of requests and I would expect premiums to stay pretty firm," said one trader.
Others countered that with the sloppy supply situation seen in the north over the past month fewer cargoes were likely to head into Northwest Europe.
